definitions.explanation: A particular time or situation when something happens. Often used in formal contexts.

examples.japanese: {折|おり}があれば{連絡|れんらく}します。
examples.english: I'll contact you if the opportunity arises.

examples.japanese: この{折|おり}にお{礼|れい}を{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: I would like to express my gratitude on this occasion.

examples.japanese: {折|おり}を{見|み}て{相談|そうだん}させてください。
examples.english: Please let me consult with you when there's an opportunity.

notes:
{折|おり} means 'occasion' or 'opportunity' and is used to refer to a suitable or noteworthy time. It has a formal, somewhat literary tone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {折|おり}があれば: if there's an opportunity
- この{折|おり}に: on this occasion
- {折|おり}を{見|み}て: when the opportunity arises, finding the right moment
- {折|おり}に{触|ふ}れて: from time to time, on various occasions
- ～の{折|おり}: at the time of ~

REGISTER:
Formal and literary. Frequent in business correspondence, speeches, and polite letters. In everyday conversation, {時|とき} or {機会|きかい} are more natural.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {時|とき}: time, when (neutral, everyday)
- {機会|きかい}: opportunity, chance (formal but more common in speech)
- {際|さい}: occasion, time of (formal, similar register to {折|おり})
